text:
Dev Patel: pulling together a quick summary of recurring SDK pain we’re seeing in support (mostly last ~4–6 weeks). Theme is “retry/timeout behavior differs per language” + hard to debug because request_id not always surfaced.

Dev Patel: Top complaint buckets (w/ examples):
1) Timeouts not honored / confusing timeout semantics
- Python streaming “hangs” beyond configured timeout, or timeout only applies to connect not read.
- Customer expects “overall request” timeout but gets per-socket behavior.

2) 429 handling inconsistent (Retry-After + backoff)
- Go SDK ignoring Retry-After; retries too fast -> perceived throttling loop.
- Some SDKs retry 429 with no jitter (thundering herd concerns).

3) Retry policy inconsistency / retries on non-retryable codes
- TS SDK allegedly retrying 400 in one case -> customer worried about duplicate billing / double submits.

4) Streaming disconnects behind enterprise proxy
- “stream ends mid-response” / half-closed connections; customers ask “should I retry?” and we don’t have consistent guidance.

Dev Patel: Linking concrete tickets so we can keep one thread for patterns:
- SUP-29410 python sdk: timeouts not honored streaming https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/SUP-29410
- SUP-29438 ts sdk: retries on 400 causing duplicate billing concern https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/SUP-29438
- SUP-29477 go sdk: missing Retry-After handling on 429 https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/SUP-29477
- SUP-29505 streaming disconnects behind proxy; retry guidance needed https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/SUP-29505

Dev Patel: Also internal ask from oncall/support: request_id needs to be in SDK errors 100% of the time (non-stream + stream):
- INT-1182 request_id not visible in sdk errors https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/INT-1182

Owen Phillips: +1. A lot of these end up being “can you send request_id?” and customer can’t find it, esp for streaming exceptions. If we can standardize “every thrown error includes request_id + retryable flag + status_code” it will cut our back and forth.

Owen Phillips: For 429s, we should explicitly ask for:
- SDK version
- config (timeout + max_retries)
- whether they see Retry-After header
- whether they’re behind proxy / corporate TLS interception

Owen Phillips: I dropped a draft macro here (WIP) but it depends on final option names across Python/TS/Go.

Support Bot: :information_source: Related internal ticket mentioned: INT-1199 update support macro: sdk retry/timeout troubleshooting https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/INT-1199

Monica Patel: thanks Dev/Owen. This lines up with the parity initiative. We should use these as acceptance criteria + for migration notes.

Monica Patel: Two immediate asks from support side:
1) Can you add the “common questions to ask” to a short runbook (even before SDK changes ship)?
2) For each ticket, can we capture current SDK language + version + whether request_id available? That will help us prove improvement post-release.

Ibrahim Khan: Yup. These are exactly the gaps we’re trying to close. We’re standardizing:
- retryable status codes (429, 500/502/503/504) + network errors
- exponential backoff + jitter; respect Retry-After (seconds + HTTP date)
- a single timeout model (overall + connect/read mapping per language)
- streaming semantics: we won’t auto-retry streaming by default; instead surface partial output + typed “disconnect” error + guidance for safe retry (idempotency)

Ibrahim Khan: Also adding consistent error fields: request_id, status_code, retryable, retry_count, timeout_ms. Should directly help INT-1182.

Allison Grant: From SRE perspective, the current behavior is risky during elevated 429s. In at least one incident review we suspected clients were retrying too aggressively without jitter. Please keep linking any “retry storm” customer notes here.

Dana Lo: Re SUP-29438: I looked at the TS repro from the ticket. It *shouldn’t* retry 400; likely we’re misclassifying an error thrown by fetch as “network” and replaying it. I’ll post back once we confirm.

Sabrina James: Re SUP-29410: Python streaming timeout: I can reproduce if user sets only “timeout=XX” and expects it to cap streaming duration; current implementation only covers connect/read in a way that isn’t obvious. We’ll align with the new timeout ADR + update docsstrings.

Mateusz Zielinski: Re SUP-29477: Go ignoring Retry-After is real in older versions; we parse it inconsistently (only int seconds, not date). Fix is queued; will also add jitter.

Dev Patel: great. For support runbook, I’ll draft a short checklist and route through @Monica Patel + @Ibrahim Khan for exact option names once the SDKs converge.

Dev Patel: Proposed interim macro content (until releases go out):
- Please share: language SDK + version, endpoint (streaming vs non-stream), region
- Please share request_id (if available) OR raw response headers if they can capture
- Please confirm whether you have retries enabled and the max attempts/backoff (if configurable)
- If streaming disconnect: are you behind a proxy? any “connection reset” logs?

Owen Phillips: + add: “If you retry streaming, you may get duplicated tokens/partial output; safest is to retry with idempotency key if your workflow supports it, or treat as best-effort.” Customers keep asking what’s “safe”.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. We should be explicit: default guidance = don’t auto-retry streaming; if app retries, do it at a higher level with idempotency key + dedupe if needed.

Monica Patel: Action items:
- Dev: draft runbook/macro + link this thread + the Jira tickets
- Ibrahim/Dana/Sabrina/Mateusz: when fixes land, please comment here with target versions so support can advise upgrades
- Allison: once telemetry fields are standardized, we’ll update macro to request “retry_count / timeout_ms / streaming_disconnect_reason” if exposed

Dev Patel: ack. I’ll keep this thread updated as more SUPs come in that match the same pattern. :thumbsup:
